title: Transit-anchored audit journal retention orchestration and WORM handoff
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a transit-anchored immutable audit journal exporter that: (1) cryptographically anchors records at ingestion time, (2) orchestrates region-aware WORM handoff with retention policy enforcement, and (3) exposes automated evidence bundles and compliance reports for auditors. The goal is to close gaps between real-time admin-event capture and long-term tamper-evident storage while preserving data residency constraints and supporting emergency legal holds.
acceptance_criteria: Audit events (admin actions, config changes, access grants) are hashed and included in a chaining header at ingress time
Exporter publishes signed manifests to a verification topic and pushes append-only blobs into customer-region WORM buckets with retention metadata
Retention engine applies per-customer residency/retention policies and prevents premature deletion; overrides require documented legal-hold workflow
Automated monthly evidence export runs and produces a downloadable bundle with integrity proofs (manifest + HSM timestamp) and a human-readable audit summary
Console shows per-route retained bytes, last anchor timestamp, and retention state; role-based access enforced for evidence retrieval
End-to-end integration tests for failover: exporter fallback to regional replica and audit continuity verified under simulated region outage
implementation_notes: Design: introduce an ingestion-side 'transit anchor' that computes a running Merkle-ish chain per-customer and emits small anchor records to KMS/HSM for notarization
Storage: use existing sealed-bucket naming conventions but add versioned retention-manifest objects (object metadata: residency, retention-until, anchor-id)

Orchestration: retention controller will be a separate component (controller pattern) that reconciles manifests and enforces retention lifecycles; it will operate with a permissioned service account able to request HSM stamps
Security: HSM signing integration using the platform KMS proxy; ensure signing keys are rotation-compatible and that key usage is logged separately

Performance trade-offs: anchor-on-write adds ~5-12ms per batched write (depends on batch size). We'll batch anchors and compress manifests to amortize cost. If strict per-record anchoring is required for a customer, expose a 'strong-anchoring' toggle but default to batch anchors for cost/latency balance.

Data residency: controller must validate target WORM buckets against customer-region mapping. If customer policy prohibits cross-region anchoring, the anchor record still stored centrally but the evidence bundle contains proof-of-local-storage via signed access logs.

Operator UX: create a lightweight runbook for emergency retention holds: validate request, create a legal-hold manifest, pin manifests to 'hold/' prefix, notify compliance channel. This should be automatable via API for SREs.

Observability: add metrics for anchor latency, anchor failure rate, manifests generated per hour, and number of retention overrides. Expose traces linking an admin event to its anchor and final WORM object ID.

Backward compatibility: exporter should accept legacy audit events and map them into new manifest schema without losing historical anchors; provide a one-time migration tool for the last 30 days of events.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: RFC posted to confluence outlining transit-anchor design and retention-controller responsibilities. Requested early feedback from Security and Legal.
2025-02-18: Security review scheduled; initial feedback: require HSM-to-audit separation and KMS key tagging for retention-sensitive tenants.
2025-02-21: Prototype implemented for per-customer chain generation in the ingestion proxy. Local tests show chain consistency under 2000 RPS.
2025-02-24: Spike on HSM stamping: integration with vendor emulator completed. End-to-end test demonstrates signed manifest created and verifiable with public key.
2025-02-27: Design review with Platform and Console teams. Decided to add a new 'evidence' API surface for downloads rather than reusing existing logs API to preserve ACL boundaries.

2025-03-01: Began implementation of retention-controller reconciliation loop and added initial unit tests. Found a race when manifest reconciliation overlaps with manual retention override; added optimistic locking plan.
2025-03-03: PR opened for ingestion-side anchor generation: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821. Awaiting Diego's review. QA plan drafted and attached.
Blockers: Access to production HSM cluster requires additional compliance training for the feature owner (scheduled 2025-03-06).
qa_results: Integration test suite (CI): 128 tests, 3 failures (timing-sensitive) — failures traced to batch-window sizing; fixed by lowering max-batch-wait in prod config
Manual verification: retrieved evidence bundle for tenant 'acme-corp' in eu-west-1; bundle contains manifest, HSM timestamp, object list, and verification key. Hashes validated against manifest

Chaos test: simulated eu-west-1 outage; exporter successfully redirected to eu-central-1 replica and created contiguous anchors. Evidence bundle contains continuity proof linking pre/post failover anchors

Performance: median additional latency for writes with default batching = 8ms at 1000 RPS; 99th percentile = 36ms. Meets configured latency SLO for audit writes but requires tuning for latency-sensitive tenants
